jobs.title: Halloween is over and a Ditmars bodega has 200 unsold pumpkins. Auntie Bee has an idea: "seasonal artisanal gourds."

options.label: Sell them as artisanal gourds
options.cost: Every buyer's trust in the word "artisanal"
options.win: Hand-lettered sign, a little straw, "locally sourced." They were sourced locally. From the bodega.
options.fizzle: A man asked which farm. You said "Queens." He walked away. So did everybody.

options.label: Sell them as pumpkins, cheap
options.win: Two for five dollars. A line of pie bakers. Auntie Bee called you "too honest for this family" and kept her cut.
options.fizzle: Nobody wants a pumpkin on November 2nd. Not even for pie.

jobs.bust: A food inspector asked to see the artisan. You pointed at a pumpkin. It did not help.
jobs.caught: Remember the artisanal gourds? A brunch blogger traced them to the bodega and tagged the 114½ for some reason.
jobs.headline: "Artisanal gourds" were bodega pumpkins, says brunch blogger. Seller: {name}.

jobs.title: Marathon Sunday. A runner from Long Island City wants a ride for "miles 14 to 22" in Tito's van. He'll pay well.

options.label: Drive him, drop him at mile 22
options.win: Eight miles in air conditioning. He jogged out at mile 22 and finished "strong." His medal photo is very sweaty for some reason.
options.fizzle: The bridge was closed for the race. Obviously. You sat in traffic with a man in short shorts for three hours.

options.label: Hand out water at mile 14 instead
options.get: Good vibes and a small tip
options.win: Two hundred cups of water, two hundred high fives. The runner tipped you anyway and ran all 26.2. Mostly.
options.fizzle: You ran out of cups at mile 14 and a half. The runners didn't care. You did.

jobs.bust: Race officials found a runner with a perfect split time and a seatbelt mark. He pointed at the van.
jobs.caught: Remember the marathon shortcut? The runner's watch tracked 31 miles an hour between miles 14 and 22. The 114½ ran the numbers.
jobs.headline: Marathon runner's "personal best" included a van. Driver: {name}.

jobs.title: A landlord wants his building's rent-stabilized paperwork "misplaced" before an inspection. Gigi knows the filing cabinet.

options.label: Misplace the paperwork
options.win: The folder is in a box marked XMAS DECORATIONS. The inspection found nothing. The tenants found out nothing. Yet.
options.fizzle: The filing cabinet was locked. Gigi had the key. Gigi was at bingo.

options.label: Make a copy for the tenants first
options.get: Pablo's fee, and a clear conscience
options.win: The folder went missing. A copy went under six doors. The landlord paid. The tenants won. Gigi winked.
options.fizzle: The copy machine jammed on page one. It always jams on page one.

jobs.bust: The inspector arrived early with a coffee and found you holding the folder over a shredder.
jobs.caught: Remember the misplaced paperwork? A tenant found the box marked XMAS DECORATIONS in October. She called the 114½ and Lola.
jobs.headline: Rent paperwork found in a Christmas box. Who put it there? {name}, says the landlord's lawyer.
